source.author: stat
source.text: nec minus haec laeti trahimus solacia, quam si praecipiti convulsa noto prospectet amicam puppis humum, iuvat ingressos felicia regni omina, quod superest fati vitaeque laborum fortuna transire tua.
source.text_original: nec minus haec laeti trahimus solacia, quam si / praecipiti convulsa noto prospectet amicam / puppis humum, iuvat ingressos felicia regni / omina, quod superest fati vitaeque laborum / fortuna transire tua.
source.text_english: And we draw these comforts no less gladly than if a ship, torn away by the headlong blast, were to look out upon friendly land; it is a delight, on entering, to pass by the happy omens of the kingdom, and whatever still remains of fate and of the labors of life is by your fortune to be passed through.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: taurea vulnifico portat celer aspera plumbo terga Lacon, saltem in vacuos ut bracchia ventos spargat et Oebalium Pagaseia puppis alumnum spectet securo celebrantem litora ludo.
reuse.text_original: taurea vulnifico portat celer aspera plumbo / terga Lacon, saltem in vacuos ut bracchia ventos / spargat et Oebalium Pagaseia puppis alumnum / spectet securo celebrantem litora ludo.
reuse.text_english: The Lacedaemonian, swift, bears on his rough back the bull’s-hide with its wound-making lead, so that at least he may scatter his arms into the empty winds and the Pagasaean ship may watch the Oebalian youth as he sports in safety, making the shore ring with his play.
